summary: Defines the Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol, an election protocol that assigns responsibility for a virtual router to one of several routers on a LAN. If the Master fails, another takes over, so hosts keep using the same default gateway address. It obsoletes RFC 2338 and was replaced by RFC 5798.

eli5.summary: Two routers share one pretend address. If the main one breaks, the backup quietly steps in so nobody notices.

subtitle: Multiple routers share one virtual address and automatically failover when the master fails.

tldr.problem: A single default router address is a single point of failure; if the router fails, all hosts using it as their default gateway become unreachable even if backup routers are available.
tldr.mechanism: VRRP is an election protocol that assigns responsibility for a virtual router IP address to one of several physical routers on a LAN. The router with the highest priority becomes the Master and forwards traffic for the virtual address. If it fails, the next highest priority router takes over automatically.
tldr.outcome: Multiple physical routers can back up a single default gateway address without requiring hosts to run routing protocols or manually switch to a backup. Hosts simply configure the virtual address as their default route and remain unaware of failovers.

today: RFC 3768 defines VRRP version 2 for IPv4 routers and is an Internet Standard. It was obsoleted by RFC 5798, which extended VRRP to support IPv6.

sections.title: The Problem: Single Point of Failure
sections.content:
End-hosts typically use a statically configured default route to reach the rest of the network. Running a dynamic routing protocol on every host is impractical due to administrative overhead, processing load, and implementation constraints. Router discovery protocols can detect lost neighbors, but they require all hosts to participate and suffer from long timeout periods that create unacceptable "black holes" when a router fails.

VRRP eliminates this single point of failure by allowing multiple routers to share a single virtual IP address. Hosts configure the virtual address as their default gateway, and one router (the Master) handles traffic. When the Master fails, another router automatically takes over, transparently restoring connectivity.
sections.eli5: If there is only one way to get somewhere and that road breaks, you are stuck. VRRP puts two roads in place so if one breaks, traffic can take the other one automatically.

sections.title: How VRRP Works
sections.content:
VRRP defines a virtual router as an abstract object identified by a Virtual Router ID (VRID) and a set of associated IP addresses. One or more physical VRRP routers on a LAN participate in each virtual router election.

The router that owns the virtual router's IP address (the IP address owner) always becomes the Master with a fixed priority of 255. Other routers configure a lower priority and act as Backups. The Master sends periodic advertisements (VRRP messages) to announce its presence. Backup routers monitor these advertisements; if they stop arriving within a timeout period, the Backup with the highest priority becomes the new Master.

To minimize unnecessary failovers, a lower-priority Backup does not preempt a higher-priority Master unless explicitly configured or the current Master fails. The protocol uses IP multicast (224.0.0.18) for all advertisements.
sections.eli5: Two routers, one main and one backup, share a pretend address. The main one keeps saying "I am here" every second. If the backup stops hearing it, the backup takes over.

sections.title: The VRRP Advertisement Packet
sections.content:
VRRP routers communicate using a single message type: the Advertisement. The message includes the virtual router ID, the sender's priority, the count of virtual IP addresses, the advertisement interval, a checksum, and the list of IP addresses the virtual router manages.

Advertisements are sent using IP protocol number 112, with a TTL (Time To Live) of 255 and the multicast address 224.0.0.18. The TTL requirement ensures that VRRP packets do not propagate beyond the local LAN; receiving a VRRP packet with TTL other than 255 indicates an error and the packet is discarded. The source MAC address of advertisements is the virtual router's MAC address (00-00-5E-00-01-{VRID}), which helps learning bridges track the virtual router's location.
sections.eli5: The message is like a postcard the master router mails every second saying "I am still here, my priority is 255, and these are the addresses I manage."

sections.title: The Master Election State Machine
sections.content:
Each VRRP router maintains a state machine with three states: Initialize, Master, and Backup. In the Initialize state, the router waits for a startup event. If the router is the IP address owner (priority 255), it immediately transitions to Master and sends an advertisement. Otherwise, it starts a timer (Master_Down_Interval) and transitions to Backup.

While in Backup state, the router does not respond to ARP requests for the virtual address and discards packets sent to it. It monitors advertisements from the Master. If an advertisement with priority 0 is received, it means the Master is voluntarily stepping down; the Backup then waits only Skew_Time before becoming Master. If advertisements stop for Master_Down_Interval seconds, the Backup transitions to Master. If a higher-priority advertisement is received, the backup resets its timer.

The Master responds to ARP requests for the virtual address and forwards traffic. If it receives an advertisement from a higher-priority router, or from another router with equal priority but a higher IP address, it transitions to Backup.
sections.eli5: The election is simple: the owner always wins. If the owner goes away, the next in line waits a moment to make sure, then takes over.

sections.title: Deployment Issues
sections.content:
VRRP interacts with ARP in important ways. When a router transitions to Master, it must send gratuitous ARP requests containing the virtual router's MAC address to update the ARP tables on the LAN. VRRP routers must not forward packets destined to the virtual address when they are not the IP address owner (unless they are the current Master), as this can cause forwarding loops on LANs where devices receive their own transmitted frames (like token ring).

The protocol defines virtual MAC address formats for different LAN types: Ethernet and standard LANs use IEEE 802 format (00-00-5E-00-01-{VRID}), token ring uses functional addresses to avoid conflicts with other protocols, and ATM LANE operation is out of scope.

Regarding security, VRRP does not provide any authentication. While earlier versions included authentication methods, operational experience showed these did not provide meaningful security since a hostile router can still create multiple masters or disrupt ARP independent of VRRP. The TTL check (requiring TTL 255) limits attacks to the local LAN.
sections.eli5: When the backup takes over, it has to tell everyone "hey, I am now answering for this address" using special messages on the network.
